title: The Last Train Home
description: The operational event version is authoritative. The primary reducer rejects stale versions and duplicate events. A replicated passenger projection is not the source timetable and must not become a competing authoritative writer. DynamoDB replication is asynchronous. Regional broadcasters consume their local streams and use local connection registries. The assumed compatible global-table/stream configuration and regional resource policies require deployment validation. Stations reauthenticate, fetch current state plus a version watermark, then reconcile deltas after reconnect. A WebSocket CONNECT authorizer and snapshot backend enforce identity; neither is fully expanded. The secondary snapshot endpoint, regional connection registries, routing/health checks and source-feed disaster recovery are omitted. The shown primary snapshot path alone is not a complete regional failover implementation. Passenger information only: no signalling or train control.

edges.meaning: Cross-account bus policy and forwarding role allow only the operational event source.
Partition by train or station according to ordering requirements; fan-in is not a global event order.
Consumer deduplicates and rejects stale authoritative versions.
Primary region is the only projection writer; records include source version and update time.
DynamoDB Streams invokes the broadcaster; retries may deliver duplicate changes.
Calls management API for registered connection IDs; regional connection store is omitted.
Pushes updates over an authenticated connection; disconnected displays can miss deltas.
Asynchronous global-table replication; the regional replica is not the timetable authority.
Regional stream drives local notifications after replicated writes arrive.
Uses the local connection registry and local API management endpoint.
After regional outage the client explicitly reconnects, reauthenticates and fetches a snapshot; existing sockets do not move.
Station identity tokens must be validated at connection and snapshot endpoints.
Client fetches full current state and a version watermark on connect/reconnect.
Snapshot backend reads current state; an API integration Lambda and secondary snapshot endpoint are omitted.
